correctness.rationale: In F_2^n modulo the all-ones vector, endpoint displacement has exactly two binary support representatives, S and its complement. The number of letters in a word is at least the size of its odd-occurrence support; equality at minimum length forces a permutation of one minimal support, and such permutations give distinct simple geodesics since the edge generators are distinct. For n>=5 a reroute replaces two consecutive letters by a different ordering of the same pair: two distinct unordered pairs with equal quotient sum would have symmetric difference all n coordinates, but it has size at most four. Thus the support is invariant, and the adjacent swaps connect each permutation component; both supports are minimal precisely for even n at distance n/2. F_3 is K_4 and has only one-step geodesics, while F_4 is K_(4,4), whose four two-step paths between equal-side endpoints differ only at their middle and form K_4. Component size, degree, inversion metric and edge count follow from the adjacent-transposition Cayley graph; S_3 gives a six-cycle in each n=6 diametric component. Each quotient vertex has binom(n,n/2)/2 diametric neighbors in even dimension, so multiplying by 2^(n-1)/2 and dividing by the total number of unordered pairs yields the exact count and fraction; the central-binomial asymptotic agrees. A separately written check enumerating vertex paths for all targets from zero in n=3 through 8 reproduced the component sizes, degrees and edge counts; relevant replay files are finite_rerouting_check.py and finite_chunk_n8.txt in the review evidence. That replay does not replace the argument for unbounded n. The frozen verifier and its recorded output for n=3 through 10 were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The classification resolves whether shortest routes stay mutually reachable after identifying antipodes, a natural stability question for a standard quotient of a cube. It determines the exact failure regime, exhibits two nontrivial components rather than isolated paths in the first disconnected instance, and explains why the smallest even-dimensional diametric example behaves differently. The constructive component metric and the frequency of affected endpoint pairs add usable quantitative conclusions.
